title: Serbia's student movement
dek: Two years after a station canopy collapse in Novi Sad killed 16 people, the student-led movement it sparked has won Serbia's snap election, ending 14 years of rule by Aleksandar Vučić's party. What the students now demand, and what happens to the investigations.
summary: On November 1, 2024, a concrete canopy at the newly renovated railway station in Novi Sad, Serbia's second-largest city, collapsed at 11:52 a.m., killing 16 people, according to AP and AFP. Many Serbians blamed corruption and negligence in state infrastructure projects, and university students led some of the country's largest protests since 2000. Thirteen people, including former construction minister Goran Vesić, were charged, but no trial has started, and the European Public Prosecutor's Office is investigating possible misuse of EU funds in the renovation.

President Aleksandar Vučić called a snap parliamentary election in September 2026. In the October 25 vote, with turnout of nearly 70 percent, the highest since 1992, the Student List defeated his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), which had governed for 14 years. Vučić conceded on election night; a CeSID-Ipsos projection gave the students 138 of 250 seats and the SNS 104, enough for the Student List to govern alone.

On November 1, 2026, thousands marked the second anniversary in Novi Sad with a silent march and 16 minutes of silence. The same day, prosecutors ordered the 48-hour detention of Marko Kričak, head of the criminal police, on suspicion of abuse of office; he denies accusations that he orchestrated violence against protesters. Students are demanding a review of the high-profile investigations, including the canopy case. Who will be prime minister has not been announced.

phases.name: The canopy collapse and two years of protest
After the victory: anniversary and investigations

events.label: confirmed
events.text: The concrete canopy of the renovated Novi Sad railway station collapses at 11:52 a.m., killing 16 people, 14 at the scene and two later, AP and AFP report. The renovation was part of a railway project with China and Hungary.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: The Student List wins Serbia's snap election, defeating Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party after 14 years in power; Vučić concedes, saying the students will have between 135 and 140 seats and his party around 105. A CeSID-Ipsos projection gives 138 seats to the students and 104 to the SNS, on turnout of nearly 70 percent, Reuters and Euronews report.

events.label: reported
events.text: The Student List, led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanović, fielded 250 largely unknown candidates, including university professors, actors and farmers; who will become prime minister is unclear, Reuters reports. "Tonight we celebrate victory. Tomorrow we build the future," said Belgrade University professor Radomir Sajčić, speaking for the students.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Thousands mark two years since the Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse that killed 16 people, with a silent march in the rain, 16 wreaths and 16 minutes of silence, AP and AFP report; students say they now want those responsible to be punished.

events.label: alleged
events.text: Prosecutors order the 48-hour detention of Marko Kričak, head of the criminal police, and another senior officer on suspicion of abuse of office linked to a murder investigation, AP reports. Kričak is accused of orchestrating violence during the student protests and of threatening a student; he denies the allegations.

events.label: reported
events.text: Belgrade's chief prosecutor says there is a well-founded suspicion that Kričak and another senior police officer abused their positions in a May 2026 murder investigation, and grounds to suspect Kričak abused a person on police premises, BBC News in Serbian reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: Serbia's Supreme Public Prosecutor's Office orders the Belgrade prosecutors to act on student complaints against criminal police chief Marko Kričak over an August 2025 incident in a Government of Serbia garage, which had gone more than a year without result, Vreme reports. The paper says Kričak, detained on November 1, was still in custody on November 3.

events.label: pending
events.text: Formation of the new government and the choice of prime minister, the outcome of the Kričak detention, and whether the stalled canopy prosecution and the EU funds investigation move forward. Still being checked.

claims.title: Who is responsible for the collapse?
claims.label: disputed
claims.a: Students and many Serbians blame corruption and negligence in state infrastructure projects; an independent expert review found the renovation was rushed under political orders and alleged a "systematic degradation of construction standards".
claims.b: Thirteen people, including a former minister, have been charged, and the cases are not yet tried; corruption suspicions around the project's finances are under separate investigation.
claims.status: No court has ruled; no trial has started.

accountability.action: 13 people, including former minister Goran Vesić, charged with a serious crime against public safety; no trial yet
